newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia firm on NATO expansion before Primakov trip.
newsitem.headline: Russia firm on NATO expansion before Primakov trip.

text.p: Russian opposition to NATO expansion plans remained "unflinching" on Monday before talks in Brussels between Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov and alliance foreign ministers, Interfax news agency said.

Interfax said Primakov, who was due to leave for Brussels on Tuesday, wanted to assess whether the Western alliance is taking account of Moscow's concerns as it discusses plans to take in new members from Eastern and Central Europe.
Primakov was also due to meet NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana before flying home on Thursday, it said.

"Yevgeny Primakov intends to find out to what extent the unofficial signals and statements that are now appearing on the alliance's readiness to take account of Russia's concerns...correspond to reality," Interfax quoted a foreign ministry source as saying.
The source said Russia's opposition to NATO expansion "remains unflinching".
A defence ministry spokesman said Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodionov would also visit Brussels soon but declined to say when.
Itar-Tass news agency said Rodionov's visit would be next week and quoted ministry sources as saying he would meet Solana and NATO defence ministers.
Western leaders have repeatedly said accession talks will start for some former communist-ruled states in Eastern and Central Europe next year, whatever Moscow's objections.

Russia says such enlargement would threaten its security. Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin reiterated those fears at a European security summit in Lisbon last week, but most other leaders backed NATO's plans.
In Brussels, diplomats said NATO foreign ministers would set a date later this week for a summit next year to invite new members to join the alliance.
But the diplomats said the ministers would also try to ease Russian fears by offering not to station nuclear weapons on the territory of any new members.
